players.product: Silicon carbide (SiC) substrates: conductive, semi-insulating and P-type (6/8-inch volume, 12-inch launched); also optical-grade SiC for micro-nano optics

quarterly_data.quarter: SICC results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual and Q1 2026 (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chairman and general manager Zong Yanmin (results briefing): Q1 2026 gross margin improved by 25% quarter on quarter from Q4 2025, as process optimisation and yield gains cut core-product costs and lean management raised efficiency; for full-year 2026 the company's focus shifts further to profitability growth. He said substrate prices have gone through a full adjustment over the past two years: 6-inch prices have entered a relatively stable range and 8-inch prices have clearly stabilised while still penetrating, with the industry moving to 'stable prices, expanding demand'; automotive-grade substrates have stayed in supply-demand balance given their high barriers, while non-automotive supply is clearing out and its prices have stabilised. The company says it will price on value and avoid involution-style price competition, and that plant utilisation is at a reasonable level this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 gross margin up 25% quarter on quarter

quarterly_data.quarter: SICC results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual and Q1 2026 (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chairman Zong Yanmin (results briefing): more than half of the global top-10 power-device makers are direct customers of the company (names confidential); it has no direct supply relationship with power-module and system makers such as SST suppliers, which sit further downstream. Its global 8-inch SiC substrate share is over 50%. It completed the full 12-inch range (conductive N-type, P-type and semi-insulating) and has received orders from leading customers; its P-type substrates for smart-grid / UHV DC applications are entering field testing; in micro-nano optics, strategic cooperation with leading optics customers has produced initial use in AR/VR and precision optical sensing; and SiC is being used as a heat-spreading substrate or packaging material for high-power chips in advanced packaging.
